jordan (Acme): Hey team — after upgrading to @redwood/ts-sdk@1.12.0 our tool calls sometimes pick the wrong tool and the API returns a 400 schema_validation_error. Happens intermittently but reproducible for our invoice OCR workflow. Posted a minimized repro below.
sophie (support): thanks — can you paste the SDK call + the request body you see in your network/logs? also which model and tool schema you registered?
jordan (Acme): minimal TS snippet — this is what we call:```ts
import Redwood from '@redwood/ts-sdk'
const client = new Redwood({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY})
await client.callTool('ocr.extract', {file: Buffer.from(pdfBytes)})
```we expect args to be an object {file: bytes, page: number?} but server sees an array and rejects:

Log (proxy capture):
POST /v1/tool-call
{
  "tool": "ocr.extract",
  "args": [
    {"file":"<base64>"}
  ]
}

Error: 400 schema_validation_error: expected object for "args" according to tool schema, got array

This started after 1.12.0 — reverting to 1.11.3 fixes it.
sophie (support): very helpful, tx. can you also attach the tool schema you have registered (the JSON that declares args shape)?
jordan (Acme): schema is:```json
{"name":"ocr.extract","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"file":{"type":"string","format":"base64"},"page":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["file"]}}
```

So server expects args to be an object.

kevin (devx): cc @ajay — this smells like the TS SDK is wrapping single positional arg into an array when the call uses the short form. Do you use the named-args overload?
ajay (eng): looking. TS SDK has two callTool signatures: callTool(name, argsObj) and callTool(name, ...positional). There was a recent change that normalizes to a unified payload but I bet optional tuple/unions changed inference. Jordan, can you show the exact compile-time call signature that your TS code resolved to?
jordan (Acme): we call exactly "callTool('ocr.extract', {file: ...})" — obvious object. no rest args.

ajay (eng): ok reproducer I ran:```ts
// repro.ts
import Redwood from '@redwood/ts-sdk'
const c = new Redwood({apiKey:process.env.KEY})
await c.callTool('ocr.extract', {file: 'YmFzZTY0'})
```node 18 + ts-node -> request body shows args: [{file:...}] for SDK@1.12.0 but SDK@1.11.3 sends args: {file:...}

Root cause (quick): the code path that serializes arguments checks for a discriminated union and treats single-field objects as a 1-tuple to support legacy positional args. A recent change to the type guards turned that check on for all object shapes when the compile-time type is inferred as a union of object|array. Type-level change caused runtime guard to coerce into array in the serializer.
sophie (support): ouch. any workaround for Acme while we patch?
ajay (eng): immediate workarounds: 1) pin to @redwood/ts-sdk@1.11.3 (confirmed) 2) call with explicit helper to force object payload:```ts
await c.callTool('ocr.extract', /*explicit*/ {__raw_args_object: true, file: '...'} )
```(we can expose a documented opt-in header) or 3) use direct REST curl to send JSON object.

kevin (devx): i'll put a warning in the upgrade docs and coordinate a quick patch release. ajay, can you own the runtime compatibility test to ensure the serializer guard only applies when the tool schema is a tuple/array?
ajay (eng): will do. Plan: revert the aggressive guard in SDK runtime and add a test matrix (object vs tuple vs union) and add schema-driven serializer (i.e., consult registered tool schema when available). Target hotfix v1.12.1 in next 24h. Creating issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/891 (internal).

jordan (Acme): thanks — pinning now. rough for prod but will hold. any ETA for patch?
ajay (eng): ETA 12-24h for patch + release. we'll post a release note and a migration blurb.

sophie (support): thanks @jordan, @ajay, @kevin. I'll keep this thread open and update the customer once the patch lands. tagging #eng-oncall if it slips. :thumbsup:

ci-bot (bot): build passed for hotfix branch (ci/patch-891) — smoke tests show requests now serialize objects properly.

sophie (support): verified with jordan that 1.12.1 fixes their case. closing once they confirm on prod. :white_check_mark:

jordan (Acme): just verified in staging with 1.12.1 — problem resolved. thanks all! :heart:
